Fixed by replacing isSourceOperand() with analyzeInsn(), which returns explicit read/write register-effect sets. Key changes: (1) whole-word token matching via regInfo() so 'edx' resolves to canonical rdx and 'rdx' never matches 'dx' — kills the r8d/edx asymmetry; (2) writes are applied AFTER reads per instruction, and xor/sub zeroing idioms are detected so 'xor rcx, rcx' clobbers without counting a param; (3) width-aware writes — an 8/16-bit destination write no longer kills the parent register, since the caller's upper bits survive; (4) mnemonic classes MOV_LIKE / READ_ONLY / READ_MODIFY_WRITE replace the substring fallthrough, incl. the 3-operand imul form and memory destinations. BUG (lifter.ts isRegister): tested 'regSize(s) > 0', but regSize() falls back to 4 for any unrecognised name, so the predicate was TRUE FOR EVERY STRING — every operand was treated as a register and immediates were lifted as registers. Fixed by adding isKnownRegister() to ir.ts (a real REG_SIZES membership test) and using that. The docstring now states explicitly why regSize() can never be used as a membership test, since the trap is invisible at the call site.

BUG (lifter.ts collectArgs32): walked backwards from the call and then called args.reverse(). Walking backwards ALREADY yields argument order — cdecl pushes right-to-left, so the push nearest the call is argument 1 — so the reverse() double-reversed and every reconstructed 32-bit call had its argument list backwards. Removed, with a comment explaining the ordering so it is not 're-fixed' back in.

Done and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. New src/pe/ordinalTables.ts holds ws2_32.dll (196), wsock32.dll (75) and oleaut32.dll (425) — 696 entries, transcribed from pefile 2024.8.26's ordlookup.

I did not take the transcription on trust. I installed pefile into a throwaway venv and diffed all 696 entries programmatically against ordlookup.ords: 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 wrong names, across all three DLLs. Counts and contents match exactly. imphash now agrees with pefile for every ordinal these tables cover, so the hashes are corpus-lookup-able.

The agent also documented that ws2_32 and wsock32 are NOT interchangeable — they disagree on ordinals 10, 11, 12 and 24 (wsock32!10 is inet_addr where ws2_32!10 is ioctlsocket) — and kept separate tables rather than aliasing. The file carries a regeneration command and a do-not-hand-edit warning.

ALSO FOUND (separate, serious — resource parser DoS): the MAX_DEPTH limit did not bound work. Each directory declares its own entry count in two uint16s, so one can claim 131070 children, and each child can point at a DISTINCT subdirectory offset that the 'visited' set cannot collapse. A 256 KB crafted .rsrc exhausted a 4 GB heap in under a minute — in a browser that is a dead tab, on a tool whose entire purpose is opening untrusted binaries. Fixed with a global MAX_TOTAL_ENTRIES budget (65536) threaded through the walk, surfaced as ResourceTree.truncated. Also clamped resource strings to 4096 chars: String.fromCharCode(...chars) with a 65535-element spread is at or over some engines' argument limit, and parseVersionInfo now keeps scanning for the terminator while capping collection so 'end' stays correct.
